newsitem.title: USA: French widow sues TWA over explosion.
newsitem.headline: French widow sues TWA over explosion.

text.p: The widow of a French passenger who was killed during the July explosion of TWA Flight 800 sued the airline and Boeing Co. on Thursday alleging that a mechanical malfunction caused the disaster.

The suit, filed in Manhattan federal court, is the third such case filed by the firm of Kreindler & Kreindler. The New York law firm is also the lead plaintiffs' counsel in litigation involving the 1988 bombing of Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie.

The current suit was brought on behalf of Catherine Dadi, whose husband Marcel was one of the 230 people killed in the July 17 explosion aboard the Paris-bound Boeing 747. It alleges that the mid-air explosion forced Dadi to endure severe mental anguish, fear of impending death and the injuries that killed him.

The claims are similar to those made in the two earlier suits filed on Monday in Brooklyn federal court. All three suits allege that a mechanical, structural and/or electrical failure caused the mid-air break-up of the airplane.
Although the suits focus on mechanical problems, they also contain a claim asking that the defendants be held liable if it is found that the explosion was caused by a bomb.

The National Transportation Board and the Federal Bureau of Investigation have said they still need more evidence before they can determine whether a bomb, a missile or a malfunction caused the explosion aboard the aircraft.

The Dadi suit alleges that the explosion was a result of TWA's "willful misconduct" for failing to properly maintain and service the airplane. It alleges that Boeing carelessly manufactured and designed the 747.

The New York Times reported on Thursday that the Federal Aviation Administration proposed a requirement 24 years ago that airlines use a technique to prevent fuel-tank explosions. The technique flushes explosive vapours from the empty space in fuel tanks by pumping in nonflammable gas.
The airline industry successfully lobbied against the proposal.

The paper reported that investigators say they believe an explosion of jet-fuel vapours burst the nearly empty centre fuel tank of the plane shortly after it took off from Kennedy International Airport.
